relevance_note: Case series of six patients with LAD-1 described individually ("six Mexican patients diagnosed with LAD-1"), two with homozygous ITGB2 variants (c.817G>A, c.295del).
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script in my scratch directory assembled the JSON and cut Table 1/Table 3 spans from the exact table lines (each checked against the table). Table 1 has patients as columns; column headers are P1-P6 (data columns 1-6). Labels: the paper uses P1-P6 (Table 1), 'Case 1'-'Case 6' (case headings) and 'Patient 1/6' (Table 3) about equally; I used P1-P6 and treated Case n and Table 3 Patient n as Pn (sex, onset and diagnosis ages agree for cases 1-4 and 6; the paper never states the mapping explicitly). Table 1 conversion is garbled: 'Parental consanguinity' cells hold two symbols each ('- -', '- +', '+ +'), the 'Deep organ abscess Omphalitis' row merges two rows ('- +', '+ +', then single symbols), 'Superficial organ abscess' is empty for P1-P3, and P1's Hepatosplenomegaly cell reads 'and sepsis -' (overflow of the Infections cell). These rows were not used except where the text states the same fact. The paper defines no legend for '+'/'-': '+' was read as present; '-' cells were left not reported (rule: undefined symbol). Consanguinity was taken from the case text only (P3, P4, P5 yes; P6 no); P1 and P2 not reported. Contradictions: (1) Table 1 shows delayed umbilical cord separation '+' for 5 patients (P1, P2, P3, P5, P6) but the Discussion says 'Three of the six patients (50%) in our study presented delayed separation of umbilical cord'; table values recorded as observed. (2) P5's Table 1 column (onset 6 days, diagnosis 1 month, consanguinity '- -', late-onset neonatal sepsis and necrotizing enterocolitis, isolates NA) does not match the Case 5 narrative (1-year-old girl of consanguineous parents with facial dermatosis, persistent ductus arteriosus at 18 months, Pseudomonas wound infection) and duplicates P6's column; both were recorded as stated, consanguinity from the text. (3) P1's case text implies death about 3 days after a third HSCT at 4 years, while the Discussion says 'one patient with LAD-1 reached a survival age of 6 years after three HSCT'; deceased_age left null. (4) Table 2 ranges (leukocytes 12-54 vs reference 6.0-17.5) sit uneasily with 'our all patients had elevated WBC and ANC', which I used as a group statement for P1, P3 (and P2 for ANC). Group statements used: 'six Mexican patients' (ethnicity, diagnosis label), 'overall outcome in our study was 100% mortality' (P3 vital status), 'We found two homozygous pathogenic variants' (pathogenicity of P1 and P6 variants). Only two patients (P1, P6) were genotyped; P2-P5 have no variant rows (diagnosed by flow cytometry). n_patients_reported = 2 (patients with an ITGB2 variant as stated); cohort_size_as_stated = 6. cites_prior_report set true from 'One patient presented autoimmune hemolytic anemia that had already been reported, 8' (P1's AIHA; Table 3 also cites ref 8 for c.817G>A), but the sentence may mean the manifestation rather than the patient. P6 variant type 'Frameshift delins' recorded as frameshift though the HGVS is a deletion. P3 'later gingivitis was analyzed' read as gingivitis observed (odd wording). P4 vasculitis is hedged in the case ('data suggestive of pulmonary vasculitis') but stated as 'ANCA-positive pulmonary vasculitis' in the Discussion for the unnamed second autoimmune patient. Omphalitis was not counted as a skin or soft tissue infection. Discussion counts without names (autoimmunity n = 2, fungal infections n = 1) excluded no one. Immunoglobulin values and microbiological isolates were not recorded as features (no interpretation given).
